title: dev-copilot — command correctness (issues, cross-addon, new-addon, finalize)
cluster_summary: Five independent spec-level defects in dev-copilot command and overlay text: the issue overlays disagree on what 'all' means, the cross-addon review uses a fixed shared /tmp path, wow-new-addon lacks Edit and implies it may push, finalize describes a push-rejection recovery that cannot work, and a stale origin/main branch remains. Every fix lands in dev-copilot alone and none routes through an upstream. Address DC-R-04, DC-R-05 and DC-R-07 (should). DC-R-12 is a cheap accuracy fix (optional). DC-A-13 is a remote branch deletion that waits for the owner's go-ahead.

verdicts.assessment: Verified. issue-audit.md:22 defines 'all' as addon repos only, while issue-summary.md:9 adds the three upstreams plus legacy wow-addon. Triaged LibKa0s issues therefore show up in the counts but no collection-wide triage or audit ever reaches them. The legacy wow-addon repo has no open issues, so its clause can go.
verdicts.remediation: Use one identical 'all' bullet in issue-audit, issue-triage, issue-summary and issue-details. It reads every row of WowAddonStandards/standards/ADDONS.md (the addon, library and docs/tooling tables) and tags each repo with its kind. Upstream rows get the base sweep only, and addon-specific checks (Lua sweep, addon check) run on addon rows only. Drop the wow-addon clause, use the same roster for repo-name matching, and align README.md:42-49.

verdicts.assessment: Verified at agent-review.md:354, 355 and 440. The fixed /tmp/roots.txt breaks the plugin's own no-fixed-shared-path rule (wow-automated-tests.md:97-100). When per-repo reviews run in parallel, one review can truncate the file while another reads it, and the collision check then reports a false clean.
verdicts.remediation: Create the file with roots=$(mktemp) before the loop and use "$roots" in the tee, cut|uniq -d and wc -l commands, including the evidence table at :440. Cite the shared-path rule.

verdicts.assessment: Verified. allowed-tools at wow-new-addon.md:4 has no Edit, and step 10 at :246 says 'if you can't push there', which implies a push the plugin forbids outside finalize (CLAUDE.md:147). That conflicts with the owner's push-authorization rule.
verdicts.remediation: Add Edit to allowed-tools. Reword step 10: edit standards/ADDONS.md in the sibling WowAddonStandards checkout on a feature branch and commit there, never push. If the checkout is absent or dirty, tell the user the row still needs adding.

verdicts.assessment: Verified at finalize.md:114. Whenever 3e has something new to push (the merge from 3d or the commit from 3c), a rejection means the histories have diverged, so --ff-only always fails. It succeeds only in the degenerate case where nothing local is unpushed, and then the push is moot. The current text is safe because it stops on failure, so fixing it only makes the spec accurate.
verdicts.remediation: On push rejection, stop that repo. Optionally git fetch to show how far origin moved, report the push output verbatim and leave the merge to the user. Never --force, rebase or merge origin in.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed. origin/main points at the initial commit d2ed30d, an ancestor of master, and the default branch is master. Nothing is lost and no MUST fails. This is a remote write, so it waits for the owner's explicit go-ahead and must not be batched in automatically.
verdicts.remediation: Only on the owner's explicit go-ahead: git push origin --delete main.
